slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
In a direct proof we start from the given facts and use definitions, postulates and earlier theorems to reach the conclusion, one justified step at a time.

A two-column proof lists statements on the left and reasons on the right. A paragraph proof tells the same chain in sentences. Example: Given AB = CD on a line in the order A, B, C, D. Prove AC = BD. Since AB = CD, add BC to both sides: AB + BC = BC + CD (addition property). By segment addition, AB + BC = AC and BC + CD = BD. So AC = BD (substitution).

slides.title: Practice
slides.html:
In a two-column proof, what must every statement have next to it?

Reveal solution

A reason: given, a definition, a postulate, a property, or a theorem already proved.

Reveal second check

Read each statement and verify that its reason is a given, definition, postulate, property or previously proved theorem.
